swallow one's pride: After the argument, Tom had to swallow his pride and say sorry to his younger sister first.
吵架之後，湯姆只好放下自尊，先向妹妹道歉。
swallow a story: Don't expect the teacher to swallow a story about a dog eating your homework; nobody believes that anymore.
別指望老師會輕信狗吃了你作業的故事，現在已經沒人相信那種說法了。
swallow one's words: He said our team would lose badly, but he had to swallow his words when we won the championship.
他說我們隊會慘敗，但當我們贏得冠軍時，他只好收回他所說的話。
swallow the cost: Instead of raising prices, the small noodle shop decided to swallow the cost of the more expensive vegetables.
這家小麵店決定自行吸收較貴的蔬菜成本，而不是調漲價格。
be swallowed up by: Many small farms near the city have been swallowed up by new apartment buildings over the past twenty years.
過去二十年來，城市附近許多小農場被新建的公寓大樓吞沒了。
a bitter pill to swallow: Losing the final game by just one point was a bitter pill to swallow for the whole team.
決賽只以一分之差落敗，對全隊來說是難以接受的事。
swallow hard: When the teacher called my name to give a speech in front of the school, I had to swallow hard.
當老師叫我的名字要我在全校面前演講時，我緊張地吞了吞口水。
swap stories: At the class reunion, we sat around the table to swap stories about our crazy high school days.
在同學會上，我們圍坐在桌旁交換關於高中瘋狂時光的故事。
swap seats: Could we swap seats on the train? I'd like to sit by the window to take some photos of the sea.
我們在火車上可以換座位嗎？我想坐在窗邊拍些海景照片。
swap places with: I would never want to swap places with a famous movie star, because they have no private life at all.
我絕對不想和電影明星交換位置，因為他們完全沒有私生活。
swap ideas: During the group project, we met in the library every Friday to swap ideas about how to design our poster.
分組報告期間，我們每週五在圖書館見面，交流如何設計海報的想法。
swap notes: After the trip to Japan, the two travelers met for coffee to swap notes on the best places to eat.
從日本旅行回來後，兩位旅人相約喝咖啡，交換關於最佳美食地點的心得。
sway public opinion: The TV ads were designed to sway public opinion in favor of the new law before the vote.
這些電視廣告的目的是在投票前左右輿論，使其支持新法案。
be swayed by emotion: When making big decisions about money, try not to be swayed by emotion; let the facts change your mind instead.
在做重大的金錢決定時，盡量不要被情緒左右，而是讓事實來改變你的想法。
sway the jury: The lawyer's moving speech helped sway the jury, and several members changed their votes at the last minute.
律師感人的演說有助於影響陪審團，幾位陪審員在最後一刻改變了他們的投票。
sway to the music: Everyone at the outdoor concert began to sway to the music, moving their arms slowly from side to side.
戶外演唱會上的每個人都開始隨著音樂搖擺，慢慢地左右揮動手臂。
hold sway: In this small village, old traditions still hold sway, and young people rarely question what the elders say.
在這個小村莊裡，古老的傳統仍然掌控一切，年輕人很少質疑長輩說的話。
swear an oath: Before starting their jobs, new police officers must swear an oath to protect the people and obey the law.
新任警察在上任前必須宣誓保護人民並遵守法律。
swear by a remedy: My grandmother swears by a remedy of hot ginger tea whenever anyone in the family catches a cold.
每當家裡有人感冒時，我奶奶對熱薑茶這個療法深信不疑。
swear off alcohol: After he got into a car accident, my uncle decided to swear off alcohol for the rest of his life.
在出了車禍之後，我叔叔決定這輩子戒酒。
swear to tell the truth: In court, every witness must raise a right hand and swear to tell the truth before answering any questions.
在法庭上，每位證人在回答任何問題之前都必須舉起右手，發誓說實話。
swear at someone: The angry driver rolled down his window and began to swear at someone in the next car using very rude words.
那位憤怒的駕駛搖下車窗，開始用非常粗魯的字眼對隔壁車上的人罵髒話。
swear someone to secrecy: Before telling me about the surprise party, Jenny wanted to swear me to secrecy so that Mom wouldn't find out.
在告訴我驚喜派對的事之前，珍妮要我發誓保密，免得媽媽發現。
swear in a president: The chief justice will swear in a president at the ceremony next week, and millions will watch it on TV.
首席大法官將在下週的典禮上為總統主持宣誓就職，數百萬人會在電視上觀看。
sweat over a problem: I don't want to sweat over a problem all night, so I'll ask my math teacher for help tomorrow morning.
我不想整晚為這個問題煩心，所以明天早上我會去請數學老師幫忙。
sweat it out: There's no air conditioner in the exam room, so we'll just have to sweat it out until the test ends.
考場裡沒有冷氣，所以我們只能熬過去，直到考試結束。
don't sweat it: Don't sweat it if you fail one quiz; you still have plenty of chances to improve your grade this term.
如果一次小考沒過，別擔心；這學期你還有很多機會提高成績。
sweat blood: The students had to sweat blood for months to prepare for the exam, studying until midnight every day.
學生們為了準備考試拚命了好幾個月，每天念書到半夜。
sweat the small stuff: Life is too short to sweat the small stuff, so stop worrying about one bad hair day.
人生苦短，不該為小事煩惱，所以別再為一天頭髮沒弄好而擔心了。
no sweat: Carrying these heavy boxes upstairs for you is no sweat, since I go to the gym every week.
幫你把這些重箱子搬上樓是小事一樁，因為我每週都上健身房。
